markers.label: the gap under the pantry door
the top of the drawer pulls
in the open on the woven sun
the far side of the bed
in the deep dark under the middle
landing light through the door crack
the cat nesting in the laundry
the cat flap to the garden
a string of fairy lights still plugged in
moonlight through a gap in the tiles

meta.flavor: Lino the colour of old custard. The cabinets hang overhead like a roof.
A granite plain sixty times your height above the floor. The toaster smells of yesterday.
Cereal boxes stand like tower blocks. Something has been weaving in the corner.
Warm, humming, dark. Everything anyone ever dropped rolls down here eventually.
Floorboards wide as roads. The books above smell of dust and somebody else’s summer.
A low, soft sky of upholstery. Coins and popcorn, the couch’s quiet tax.
A red plain with a woven sun in the middle. Nowhere to hide but under the coffee table.
Terracotta tiles and the giant front door. The mail slot is a letterbox-shaped moon.
Brick towers, a wooden railway and a sleeping giant who keeps everything.
Slats overhead like the ribs of a whale. This is where lost toys go to be found.
A cupboard of bottles taller than towers. The U-bend drips like a slow clock.
Last night’s supper was never cleared. Plates like frozen lakes, a fork like a fallen tower.
A week of clothes in a heap by the basket. Pockets full of forgotten things.
Cold concrete, oil stains like lakes. Screws lie about like felled trees.
A steel shelf of jars and tins. Everything the family ever meant to fix is up here.
Beams, boxes, and the family’s forgotten past. Treasure, if you can find it in the dark.
Eleven months of the year the decorations sleep up here. Baubles big as houses glint in the dark.
